newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SURGICAL FILES SUIT AGAINST CIRCON.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SURGICAL FILES SUIT AGAINST CIRCON.

text.p: U.S. Surgical Corp said Wednesday it sought a court order to force Circon Corp, for which it has made a $16.50 per share hostile takeover bid, to hold its 1997 annual meeting.

The diversified surgical products company filed the lawsuit in the Court of Chancery in Delaware. Under Delaware law shareholders can call an annual meeting if a company fails to do so within 13 months. Circon's last annual meeting was July 12, 1996.
U.S. Surgical originally bid $18 a share for Circon, then lowered its bid to $14.50 a share and started its tender offer of $16.50 a share August 5.

U.S. Surgical also said Wednesday it reinstated a lawsuit against Circon in the same court, asking Circon to provide U.S. Surgical with information so it can communicate directly with Circon's shareholders concerning its tender offer, proxy contest and shareholders resolution.

U.S. Surgical, which owned about 14.8 percent of Circon's stock as of August 5, has proposed a non-binding shareholders resolution that calls for a prompt sale of the company and is in a proxy contest to elect two directors to Circon's board.

Delaware state law allows shareholders to call an annual shareholders meeting if the company hasn't done so in the last 13 months. Circon, a Delaware corporation, held its last annual meeting July 12 1996.
A Circon spokesman said the company has scheduled a shareholders meeting for October 6. He added Circon's board is reviewing U.S. Surgical's latest offer and will make a statement by August 19.
Circon's stock rose 3/16 to 15-3/4 Wednesday afternoon.
